title: Lumibricks reviews in: Neon Elite Lounge and Neon Garden shine (mostly)
summary: Brick Fanatics has reviewed Lumibricks' latest cyberpunk sets, the Neon Elite Lounge and Neon Garden, praising the light integration but flagging a rough minifigure-building experience.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has published a review of two new sets from compatible brick brand Lumibricks: the Neon Elite Lounge and the Neon Garden. Both are part of Lumibricks' cyberpunk collection and are designed to be displayed together, adding more greenery to the cyberpunk city theme than previous sets. The Neon Elite Lounge is the larger of the pair, going for a denser but shorter build than is typical for the range.

The review awarded the sets 6/10 overall, with a breakdown of 9/10 for design, 7/10 for playability, 8/10 for value, 2/10 for minifigures, and 6/10 for build. Reviewers highlighted the light integration as a standout feature, along with a detailed and accessible interior and other unique elements beyond the lighting. On the downside, the review criticised a fiddly light installation process, a poor figure-building experience, and noted that some of the best details end up hidden with no way to access them.

The sets are said to be part of Lumibricks' cyberpunk collection expanding "later this year," though exact release timing and pricing weren't detailed in the source material.

## Why it matters
Lumibricks has built a reputation in the compatible brick space for creative light integration, and this cyberpunk collection is being called one of the brand's strongest. For fans who enjoy display builds, city dioramas, or lighting techniques, this pairing could be a notable addition to a collection — provided you're prepared for a tricky light install and underwhelming figures.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for official release dates and pricing for the Neon Elite Lounge and Neon Garden, plus any updates on whether Lumibricks addresses the minifigure-building complaints in future sets.
